newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan crop growth a week ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan crop growth a week ahead of average.

text.p: Saskatchewan crop growth was rated a week ahead of the five-year 1992/96 average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.

Fifty five percent of spring cereals were at or past the shotblade stage, ahead of the average 42 percent. Eighty percent of flax was past the tillering stage, also ahead of the average of 67 percent. Canola was 46 percent at or past the flowering stage, well ahead of the 27 percent average.
Fifty four percent of fall cereals were in the dough stage versus the average of 46 percent. Pulse crops were 37 percent past flowering versus 12 percent last week.

Rainfall alleviated dry conditions in the southeast with crop production likely to rebound but at levels below average. West central Saskatchewan also needed more rain to keep crop potential from slipping.
An average 34 mm (1.3 inches) of rain fell on the southern grainbelt and up to 100 mm (4 inches) near Carnduff and Alida.
Topsoil moisture improved with 30 percent of crop reporters rating land poor to fair this week compared to 70 percent the week before.
Central Saskatchewan reported an average of 19 mm (0.7 inch) of rain, but Imna and Kenaston saw 50 mm (2 inches).
Topsoil moisture deteriorated slightly in the past week.
Northern districts saw an average 6 mm (0.2 inch) Topsoil moisture deteriorated in the past week.
